html:
The federal constitution of 1848 turned Switzerland from a loose league of cantons into a federal state, with Bern as the seat of government.

It followed the Sonderbund War. Its two-chamber parliament, one house by population and one with two seats per canton, was modelled on the United States. A seven-member Federal Council shared executive power. The new state took over customs, the post and coinage, which made one market of the country.

The revision of 1874 added the optional referendum, and in 1891 citizens won the right to propose amendments by popular initiative. This direct democracy, with votes several times a year, is the most distinctive feature of Switzerland. The constitution was rewritten in 1999. Women gained the vote only in 1971, through the same system of votes by men. It was part of the wave of 1848.
sum: The federal constitution of 1848 turned Switzerland from a loose league of cantons into a federal state, with Bern as the seat of government.
